blocks.body: Each state decides for itself who is a resident, and a move year usually means a part-year resident return in each state. If you are leaving a high-tax state, the burden of proving you left often falls on you, so keep evidence of the move (lease or deed, driver's license, voter registration). Keeping a home in the old state and spending many days there can make you a resident of both under some states' rules, and stock awards earned while you worked there may still be taxed there when they vest.
blocks.plain: Each state decides for itself who counts as a resident. The year you move, you usually file a part-year resident return in each state. If you're leaving a high-tax state, you often have to prove you left, so keep proof of the move — a lease or deed, driver's license, voter registration. In some states, keeping a home in your old state and spending many days there can make you count as a resident of both. Stock awards you earned while working there may still be taxed by that state when they vest.

blocks.body: A permanent move to a new area where your plan is not offered is a Marketplace special enrollment trigger (60 days), but the window generally requires that you had qualifying coverage on at least one day in the 60 days before the move. Employer plans may have different networks in the new state. Medicaid does not transfer between states, and eligibility rules differ, so apply in the new state right away. On Medicare, moving out of your Medicare Advantage or drug plan's area opens a special enrollment period.
blocks.plain: A permanent move to an area where your plan isn't offered lets you sign up for a new Marketplace plan within 60 days. To use this window, you usually must have had qualifying health coverage on at least one day in the 60 days before you moved. Job-based plans may have a different network of doctors in the new state. Medicaid doesn't carry over to a new state, and the rules for who qualifies can be different there, so apply in your new state right away. If you have Medicare, moving out of your Medicare Advantage or drug plan's area gives you a special window to pick a new plan.

The move SEP generally requires qualifying coverage on at least one day in the 60 days before the move

The 'when' label (Within 60 days of the move) still fits the Marketplace window; the Medicare window runs 2 full months from the move (Medicare.gov), Medicaid is 'right away'.

blocks.body: Auto insurance requirements and prices are set state by state, so the policy has to be re-written for the new state. Check that liability limits still match your assets rather than the new state's minimum. Also price uninsured and underinsured motorist coverage, which pays for your own injuries when the at-fault driver has no or too little insurance. Some states run low-cost auto programs for drivers with low incomes.
blocks.plain: Each state sets its own auto insurance rules and prices, so your policy must be rewritten for the new state. Make sure your liability limits still fit what you own, not just the new state's minimum. Also get a price on uninsured and underinsured motorist coverage. It pays for your own injuries when the driver who caused the crash has no insurance or not enough. Some states have low-cost car insurance programs for people with low incomes.

blocks.body: The federal moving-expense deduction is not available to most taxpayers (it remains for active-duty military moving under orders and, from 2026, for intelligence-community employees relocating on a change of assignment). For everyone else, employer-paid moving costs are taxable wages.
blocks.plain: Most people can't deduct moving costs on their federal taxes (active-duty military moving under orders still can, and from 2026 so can intelligence-community employees who relocate for a new assignment). For everyone else, if your employer pays for your move, that counts as taxable pay.

blocks.body: Wills, powers of attorney and healthcare directives are governed by state law. Documents valid where they were signed are usually honored, but a review in the new state catches execution formalities and agent-designation differences. A move into or out of a community-property state can also change how a married couple's property is treated. If cost is a barrier, legal aid offices may help if your income is low, and some states publish official fill-in forms for a simple will.
blocks.plain: Wills, powers of attorney and healthcare directives follow state law. Papers that were valid where you signed them usually still count, but having them reviewed in your new state catches differences in signing rules and in how agents are named. Moving into or out of a community-property state can also change how a married couple's property is treated. If cost is a problem, legal aid offices may help if your income is low, and some states have official fill-in forms for a simple will.

new_claims.claim: Keeping a home in a former state and spending many days there can leave a mover taxable there as a resident under some states' rules (New York: permanent place of abode for substantially all the year plus 184 days); equity awards earned while working in a state may be taxed by it at vesting after the holder moves away (California: RSU wage income sourced to California workdays from grant to vesting)

Both are state-specific; the block says 'some states' and names neither. Persona finding CFP-28. Note for the checker: 4 U.S.C. §114(a) bars a former state from taxing a nonresident's qualified-plan, IRA, 403(b), 457 and governmental-plan income, so the reviewer's 'deferred pay ... may still be taxed there' was not carried into the text.

draft.title: Update payroll withholding and your address
draft.body: Tell payroll the date you move so it can stop withholding for the old state and start withholding for the new one if it has an income tax; the new state may use its own withholding form. Give the IRS your new address on your next return or with Form 8822, and update it with every bank, brokerage and retirement-plan account. If you already get Social Security benefits, update your address with Social Security too.
draft.plain: Tell your payroll office the date you move so it can stop taking out tax for your old state and start taking out tax for your new state, if it has an income tax. Your new state may have its own withholding form to fill out. Give the IRS your new address on your next tax return or on Form 8822, and update it with every bank, brokerage and retirement account. If you already get Social Security benefits, update your address with Social Security too.
